Sean — final update and remediation summary.

What happened (root cause):
- During a label migration on Apr 18 the quota-assignment job incorrectly matched a group label, which resulted in ~28 MedAnalytics projects being bound to a default low-throughput quota pool. When their clients increased short-lived concurrent calls at 08:45 PST the combined per-org counting pushed the default pool beyond its threshold and the rate limiter returned 429s. This created a retry cascade on MedAnalytics' side.

What we did (mitigation):
- At 09:10 on Apr 18 we performed a targeted reassignment of the affected project IDs back into your high-throughput pool.
- We temporarily increased per-project burst allowances for your org for a 4-hour window to clear retries in flight.
- Enabled prefix-level KV caching for your top callers and deployed a conservative backoff override to dampen client retries at 09:20.
- Monitored traffic until 10:05; error rate returned to baseline (<1%).

Permanent fixes and follow-up actions:
- We fixed the label-migration mapping logic and added a unit test + integration check to prevent group-label collapse into default pools.
- Added a pre-apply dry run that flags >5 projects changing pool assignment in one batch for human review.
- CS will offer a follow-up call to walk your SRE team through safe retry strategies and to update onboarding docs for project labeling.

Offer: As a gesture for the outage impact on your demo, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equivalent to 1 week's average usage under this account. Monica from CS will reach out with the credit details and scheduling for a post-incident review.

Attachments included: quota-mapping.csv (before/after), error_dump_20270418.log.

If anything else pops up, flag me directly — apologies again for the disruption and thanks for your patience.
